2M.13 Praise and extol the LORD in the congregation of the people and among the multitude.

precepts.text: Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: cuz we have not been rejoicing in our creator, we've been rejoicing in the white man. Let the children of Zion be joyful in their King: for so long we've been joyful in the white man. For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he don't take pleasure in all races on the planet, only in his people. Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds. That's the rest right there.
precepts.point: I will seek that which was lost: that's our people. And bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken: we were broken. And will strengthen that which was sick: we're the sick ones. But I will destroy the fat and the strong: I'm going to destroy the nations. I will feed them with judgment.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Praise ye the Lord. Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise in the congregation of saints.” The saints are the twelve tribes God gathers.

“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him”: because we have not been rejoicing in our creator, we've been rejoicing in the white man. “let the children of Zion be joyful in their King”: for so long we've been joyful in the white man.

“For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.” He doesn't take pleasure in all races on the planet, only in his people.

“Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.” That's the rest right there. It is what Ezekiel promised the gathered sheep: “there shall they lie in a good fold, and in a fat pasture shall they feed upon the mountains of Israel. I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord God.”

precepts.text: Solomon assembled the elders of Israel to bring up the ark out of the city of David, which is Zion; Zion is another word for Jerusalem or Israel.
precepts.point: Zion is another word for Jerusalem or Israel. Jerusalem or Israel was a people before it was a place, so when scripture refers to Zion it points to the children of Israel.

note.label: Psalm 149: The High Praises and a Two-Edged Sword

precepts.why:
“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.” Solomon assembled the elders of Israel to bring up the ark of the covenant “out of the city of David, which is Zion.” Zion is another word for Jerusalem or Israel. Jerusalem or Israel was a people before it was a place, so when scripture refers to Zion it points to the children of Israel.

The King the children of Zion are joyful in is the same horn of his people, the horn of salvation, which is Christ. He will beautify the meek with salvation; meek means submissive or obedient, so if you keep the commandments and are obedient to the Most High you will have salvation. Then come the high praises in the mouth and a twoedged sword in the hand: the honour the saints, the children of Israel, receive when they overcome these people is the privilege of binding their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron. If you do not understand that we are Israelites, you will read this and think it is talking about a time during David or during the kings, but it is talking about the future.

precepts.text: Let Israel rejoice in Him that made him, for the Most High will beautify the meek with salvation; the meek is Israel.
precepts.point: The eyes of the blind shall see out of their obscurity, and the blind are Israel, like the obscurity of thinking Esau is white when he is red; the meek shall increase their joy in the Most High.

note.label: Isaiah 29: Woe to Ariel and the Sealed Book

precepts.why:
“The meek also shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.” Who are the meek? “Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.” “For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.” The meek is Israel, the people the Most High takes pleasure in and will beautify with salvation.

So all of it is about Israel. The deaf that “hear the words of the book” are Israel, in a spiritual deep sleep now beginning to wake and hear the word of God rightly. The blind whose eyes “shall see out of obscurity” are Israel, coming out of an obscurity like thinking Esau is white when he is red. And the meek who increase their joy in the Most High are Israel, rejoicing in him that made them.
